vocabulary.definition: a traditional story sometimes popularly regarded as historical but unauthenticated.
vocabulary.example: The legend of King Arthur has been passed down for generations.

vocabulary.definition: to take someone as a prisoner, especially using force.
vocabulary.example: The soldiers captured the enemy spies during the night.

vocabulary.definition: a person who is the legal property of another and is forced to obey them.
vocabulary.example: Slavery was abolished in many countries in the 19th century.

vocabulary.definition: to convert or seek to convert someone to Christianity.
vocabulary.example: The missionaries traveled to remote villages to evangelize the indigenous people.

vocabulary.definition: all the inhabitants of a particular town, area, or country.
vocabulary.example: The population of the city increased significantly over the last decade.

vocabulary.definition: a person acknowledged as holy or virtuous and regarded in Christian faith as being in heaven after death.
vocabulary.example: Saint Francis of Assisi is known for his love of animals and nature.
